newsitem.title: USA: US FCC conditionally okays Nextwave PCS licenses.
newsitem.headline: US FCC conditionally okays Nextwave PCS licenses.

text.p: Regulators Friday granted NextWave Personal Communications Inc 63 licenses it won to offer a new generation of cellular telephone service, but ordered the company to reduce its level of foreign ownership.

The company, a unit of privately held NextWave Telecom Inc, bid a total of $4.7 billion last year at two Federal Communications Commission auctions of airwave permits to provide personal communications services.

Nextwave was the No. 1 bidder. But the bids were later challenged by two unsuccessful bidders, Antigone Communications LP and PCS Devco Inc. They argued that foreign ownership of Nextwave exceeded a 25 percent federal cap.
The FCC approval was conditioned on NextWave's restructuring its finances within six months so the company no longer exceeds the foreign ownership limit.
"The arguments advanced in this proceeding raised difficult legal and financial issues," said Michele Farquhar, head of the FCC's wireless bureau.
"But having reviewed all the evidence, we believe that the decision to award these licenses on a conditional basis best serves the public interest and encourages new competition."

PCS technology is expected to make the wireless phone a mass-market product, giving consumers several different communications services -- such as phone, paging, fax and Internet access -- through a hand-held device.
Nextwave said its licenses cover 40 of the top 50 markets in the nation, including New York, Los Angeles, Boston, Washington and Houston.
Meanwhile, the company hopes to complete two securities offerings in the first quarter, if market conditions permit.
The company has registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission to sell $150 million to $200 million worth of stock and $300 million to $400 million of high-yield debt instruments.
